steps.title: Health
steps.body: is a state of physical and mental wellbeing, not just the absence of disease. Diseases can be communicable (can be passed between individuals) or non-communicable (cannot be passed on). Risk factors increase the likelihood of developing a non-communicable disease.

steps.title: Health
steps.body: is defined by the WHO as "a state of complete physical, mental and social wellbeing and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity." This means health is about more than just not being ill - it includes mental health, social wellbeing and physical fitness.

steps.title: Physical and mental health are linked.
steps.body: A person with a long-term physical illness is more likely to suffer from depression. A person with a mental health condition may neglect their physical health, leading to further problems.

steps.title: Communicable diseases
steps.body: can be passed from person to person (they are infectious, caused by pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists). Non-communicable diseases cannot be passed between people - they develop over time and are often linked to lifestyle or genetic factors.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Define the term "health." (1 mark) | Explain the difference between a communicable disease and a non-communicable disease. Give one example of each. (3 marks) | Explain the difference between a benign tumour and a malignant tumour. (3 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: The WHO definition of health includes "physical, mental and social wellbeing" - learn all three parts Never say a risk factor "causes" a disease - say it "increases the risk of" or "is linked to" the disease For causation vs correlation, always explain that correlation does NOT prove causation and suggest a possible confounding factor Benign = stays in one place; malignant = spreads (metastasis) - this is the key difference examiners look for When asked about cancer, mention uncontrolled cell division AND the formation of tumours For disease interactions, the HIV/immune system example is the most common one on exams Lifestyle factors are choices you CAN change; genetic and age factors you CANNOT change - distinguish between these in answers Remember that having a risk factor does NOT mean
